```{ojs}
{
  const a = DC.find(d => d.sec === "all" && d.weights === "unweighted");
  const g = m => SP.find(d => d.sec === "all" && d.level === "all" && d.weights === "unweighted" && d.measure === m && d.method === "cf" && d.gfe === "ext_group");

Because staff respond to enrollment less than one for one, the fall raised staff per student. Faculty FTE per student rose ${f1(f.rise)} points: ${f1(f.enrollment_part)} from the enrollment change and <b>${f1(f.beyond)}</b> beyond it. Non-faculty FTE per student rose ${f1(n.rise)}: ${f1(n.enrollment_part)} from the enrollment change and <b>${f1(n.beyond)}</b> beyond it. <b>Growth beyond enrollment is mostly non-faculty.</b></div>`;
}
```

::: {.cs-box}
#### How the instrument works
For each college, a gravity model gives the share of its students that comes from each county, based on distance and competing colleges. The instrument is the number of young people in those counties, built by aging each county's 10-year-olds forward, so current students' own choices never enter it. Its change over time is a demand shift the college does not control. The sample is the **1,903 surviving (S11) institutions** with the instrument; that is why its rises in staff per student (faculty FTE 11.0, non-faculty FTE 17.3) differ slightly from those for all 2,038 S11 institutions on the [Enrollment](../enrollment/index.qmd) page (11.0 and 17.1).
:::

```{ojs}
viewof wt2 = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Typical institution", "unweighted"], ["Weighted by FY2013 enrollment", "FY2013 FTE"]]), {value: param("w", "0") === "1" ? "FY2013 FTE" : "unweighted", label: "Average"})
```

## Predicted vs actual enrollment

```{ojs}
viewof psec = Inputs.select(["all", ...SECTORS.map(s => s.k)], {format: k => k === "all" ? "All sectors" : SECL[k], value: param("sector", "all"), label: "Sector"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("sector", psec === "all" ? null : psec); setParam("w", wt2 === "unweighted" ? null : "1");
  const r = GP.filter(d => d.sec === psec && d.weights === wt2);
  const S3 = ["Actual", "Predicted by population", "Population + national cycle"];
  const pts = r.flatMap(d => [{fy: d.fy, s: S3[0], v: d.actual, n: d.n}, {fy: d.fy, s: S3[1], v: d.population, n: d.n}, {fy: d.fy, s: S3[2], v: d.population + d.cycle, n: d.n}]);
  const c = psec === "all" ? BLUE : SECC[psec];
  const narrow = width < 640;
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 360, marginRight: narrow ? 10 : 200, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {...yearAxis, domain: [2013, 2024]}, y: {grid: true, label: "Change in log fall FTE since FY2013 (×100)"},
    color: {domain: S3, range: [c, INK, GRAY], legend: narrow},
    marks: [Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: INK}), Plot.rectX([{a: 2020.5, b: 2022.5}], {x1: "a", x2: "b", fill: SHADE}),
      Plot.lineY(pts.filter(d => d.s !== S3[0]), {x: "fy", y: "v", stroke: "s", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "5,3"}),
      Plot.lineY(pts.filter(d => d.s === S3[0]), {x: "fy", y: "v", stroke: "s", strokeWidth: 2.8}),
      narrow ? null : Plot.text(pts, Plot.selectLast({x: "fy", y: "v", z: "s", text: d => `${d.s} ${s1(d.v)}`, dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: INK})),
      Plot.tip(pts, Plot.pointer({x: "fy", y: "v", title: d => `${d.s}, FY${d.fy}: ${s1(d.v)}\n${d.n} institutions`}))]
  });
}
```

::: {.cs-note}
Predicted by population: the sector's first-stage coefficient times each college's change in the gravity population instrument (base 2002), averaged. National cycle: the sector's time-series response to the national unemployment rate (an upper bound, because federal aid and GI Bill changes moved with the cycle). Shaded: the COVID falls. Sample: 1,903 S11 groups present in FY2013 and FY2024 (each year averages the groups reporting that year). FY2024 NCES provisional.
:::

## Why enrollment fell, by sector

```{ojs}
{
  const PARTS = [["demographic", "Population"], ["cycle_national", "National cycle (upper bound)"], ["cycle_local", "Local cycle"], ["residual", "Everything else (residual)"]];
  const order = [{k: "all", l: "All sectors"}, ...SECTORS];
  const lab = Object.fromEntries(order.map(d => [d.k, d.l]));
  const r = DC.filter(d => d.weights === wt2);
  const long = r.flatMap(d => PARTS.map(([k, l]) => ({sec: lab[d.sec], part: l, v: d[k], tot: d.dlog_fte, n: d.n})));
  const narrow = width < 640;
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 50 + order.length * 34, marginLeft: narrow ? 120 : 150, marginRight: 30,
    x: {grid: true, label: "Change in log fall FTE, FY2013–24 (×100)"}, y: {domain: order.map(d => d.l), label: null},
    color: {domain: PARTS.map(p => p[1]), range: ["#2a78d6", "#eda100", "#c3ccd5", "#6250d6"], legend: true},
    marks: [Plot.barX(long, Plot.stackX({y: "sec", x: "v", fill: "part", inset: 0.5})), Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: INK}),
      Plot.dot(r, {y: d => lab[d.sec], x: "dlog_fte", r: 5, fill: "white", stroke: INK, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.tip(r, Plot.pointerY({y: d => lab[d.sec], x: "dlog_fte", title: d => `${lab[d.sec]} (${d.n} institutions)\ntotal ${s1(d.dlog_fte)}\npopulation ${s1(d.demographic)}\nnational cycle ${s1(d.cycle_national)}\nlocal cycle ${s1(d.cycle_local)}\nresidual ${s1(d.residual)}\nonline growth kept ${f1(d.online_offset)} points`}))]
  })}<p class="cs-note">Ring: the total change. Hover for each part and for the online offset (the part of total enrollment kept by growth in exclusively online students). Population added a little in most sectors; the decline is mostly the residual: competition, prices, the labor market for young adults, and choices colleges and students made.</p>`;
}
```

## How staffing responds to enrollment

An elasticity of 1 means staff move one for one with enrollment, keeping staff per student constant. Below 1, a falling enrollment raises staff per student. The default shows faculty FTE and non-faculty FTE together (full-time + one-third of part-time; faculty excludes graduate assistants).

```{ojs}
CATK = ["pair", "facfte", "nonfacfte", "allftex", "ftfac", "ptfacx", "ga", "ptshare", "facfte4", "facfte2", "total", "nonfac", "eamproffte", "nonproffte", "eamprof", "nonprof"].filter(k => k === "pair" || EL.some(d => d.outcome === k))
viewof cat = measSelect(CATK, {value: param("cat", "pair"), label: "Staff measure"})
viewof bse = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Main (county base 1987)", "b1987"], ["Robustness (base 2002, FY2006+)", "b2002"]]), {value: param("base", "b1987"), label: "Instrument"})
viewof ge = Inputs.toggle({label: "Institution × survey-era effects (where both exist)", value: param("ge", "0") === "1"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("cat", cat === "pair" ? null : cat); setParam("base", bse === "b1987" ? null : bse); setParam("ge", ge ? "1" : null);
  const CS = cat === "pair" ? PAIR : [cat];
  const POOLED = new Set(["total", "facfte", "nonfacfte", "allftex"]);
  const order = ["all", ...SGROUPS.map(s => s.k)];
  const pickRow = (sg, m) => { const r = EL.filter(d => d.outcome === m && d.base === bse && d.sg === sg); return (ge ? r.find(d => d.gfe === "group_era") : null) ?? r.find(d => d.main === 1) ?? r[0]; };
  const r = order.flatMap(sg => CS.map(m => pickRow(sg, m))).filter(d => d && d.fs_F >= 20 && (POOLED.has(d.outcome) || d.sg !== "all"))
    .map(d => ({...d, l: SGL[d.sg], lo: d.coef - 1.96 * d.se, hi: d.coef + 1.96 * d.se}));
  const narrow = width < 640;
  const share = cat === "ptshare";
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 860), height: 60 + order.length * (cat === "pair" ? 50 : 40), marginLeft: narrow ? 120 : 200, marginRight: 90,
    x: {grid: true, label: share ? "Change in part-time share per log point of fall FTE (95% interval)" : "Elasticity of staff to fall FTE (95% interval)", domain: [Math.min(-0.2, d3.min(r, d => d.lo) ?? 0), Math.max(share ? 0.5 : 2, d3.max(r, d => d.hi) ?? 1)]}, y: {domain: order.map(k => SGL[k]), label: null},
    marks: [share ? null : Plot.ruleX([1], {stroke: BREAKC, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}), Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#bbb"}),
      ...CS.map((m, i) => { const rr = r.filter(d => d.outcome === m), off = CS.length > 1 ? (i === 0 ? -6 : 6) : 0, open = CS.length > 1 && i === 1; return [
        Plot.ruleY(rr, {y: "l", x1: "lo", x2: "hi", dy: off, stroke: d => SGC[d.sg], strokeWidth: 3, strokeOpacity: open ? 0.55 : 1}),
        Plot.dot(rr, {y: "l", x: "coef", dy: off, r: 6, fill: d => open ? "white" : SGC[d.sg], stroke: d => SGC[d.sg], strokeWidth: 2}),
        Plot.text(rr, {y: "l", x: "hi", dy: off, text: d => `${CS.length > 1 ? (i === 0 ? "faculty " : "non-faculty ") : ""}${f2(d.coef)}`, dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: INK})]; }).flat(),
      Plot.tip(r, Plot.pointerY({y: "l", x: "coef", title: d => `${d.l}, ${MEASL[d.outcome]}: ${f2(d.coef)} (SE ${f2(d.se)})\n${d.gfe === "group_era" ? "institution × survey-era effects" : "institution effects"}\nfirst-stage F ${f1(d.fs_F)}${d.fe_coef != null && isFinite(d.fe_coef) ? `\nwithin-institution OLS ${f2(d.fe_coef)}` : ""}\nN ${f0(d.N)}`}))]
  })}<p class="cs-note">${cat === "pair" ? "Filled dot: faculty FTE; open dot: non-faculty FTE. " : ""}Red dashed line: elasticity 1. Private sectors are not shown: their first stages are too weak (F below 20) to report. "All institutions" pools sectors with sector × year effects and is shown for faculty FTE, non-faculty FTE, all FTE and headcount. Faculty FTE responds about 0.8 in all three public sectors; non-faculty FTE carries the sector gradient (public research highest, community colleges lowest). Part-time faculty, graduate assistants, the part-time share and executive, professional and nonprofessional staff use institution × survey-era effects because of the 2012–13 redesign. The part-time share does not respond in any public sector. Graduate-assistant estimates are noisy and change sign across specifications; read them as descriptive. EAM + professional estimates are not robust across instrument bases, so there is no national "sticky administrators" pattern.</p>`;
}
```

## Why staff per student rose, by sector

```{ojs}
SPK = ["pair", "facfte", "nonfacfte", "allftex", "ftfac", "ptfacx", "ga", "facfte4", "facfte2", "total", "nonfac"].filter(k => k === "pair" || SP.some(d => d.measure === k))
viewof dm = measSelect(SPK, {value: param("dm", "pair"), label: "Staff measure"})
viewof meth = Inputs.select(new Map([["Control function, pooled (headline)", "cf"], ["Within-institution (FE) elasticity, pooled", "fe"], ["2SLS elasticity (base 2002), pooled", "iv"], ["FE elasticity, sector-specific", "fe_sec"], ["2SLS elasticity, sector-specific", "iv_sec"]]), {value: param("meth", "cf"), label: "Elasticity used"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("dm", dm === "pair" ? null : dm); setParam("meth", meth === "cf" ? null : meth);
  const DS2 = dm === "pair" ? PAIR : [dm];
  const order = [{k: "all", l: "All sectors"}, ...SECTORS];
  const lab = Object.fromEntries(order.map(d => [d.k, d.l]));
  const wOK = wt2 === "unweighted" || (DS2.every(m => m === "total") && meth === "cf");
  const ww = wOK ? wt2 : "unweighted";
  const r = SP.filter(d => d.weights === ww && d.method === meth && d.gfe === "ext_group" && (d.level === "all" || d.level === "sector") && DS2.includes(d.measure))
    .map(d => ({...d, sl: lab[d.sec], ml: dm === "pair" ? PAIRL[d.measure] : MEASL[d.measure]}));
  const P2 = ["Elasticity below 1 meets the enrollment change", "Staff growth beyond enrollment"];
  const long = r.flatMap(d => [{...d, part: P2[0], v: d.enrollment_part}, {...d, part: P2[1], v: d.beyond}]);
  const ML = [...new Set(r.map(d => d.ml))];
  const narrow = width < 640;
  return html`${Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 50 + order.length * ML.length * 26, marginLeft: narrow ? 120 : 150, marginRight: 60,
    x: {grid: true, label: "Change in log staff per student, FY2013–24 (×100)"}, fy: {domain: order.map(d => d.l), label: null}, y: {domain: ML, label: null, axis: ML.length > 1 ? "right" : null},
    color: {domain: P2, range: [LIGHT, BLUE], legend: true},
    marks: [Plot.barX(long, Plot.stackX({fy: "sl", y: "ml", x: "v", fill: "part", inset: 0.5})), Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: INK}),
      Plot.dot(r, {fy: "sl", y: "ml", x: "rise", r: 5, fill: "white", stroke: INK, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text(r, {fy: "sl", y: "ml", x: d => Math.max(d.rise, d.enrollment_part + Math.max(0, d.beyond), d.beyond), text: d => s1(d.rise), dx: 10, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fill: INK}),
      Plot.tip(r, Plot.pointerY({fy: "sl", y: "ml", x: "rise", title: d => `${d.sl}, ${d.ml} (${d.n} institutions)\nrise ${s1(d.rise)}\n= enrollment part ${s1(d.enrollment_part)}\n+ beyond enrollment ${s1(d.beyond)}\nelasticities ${f2(d.b_demog)} (population) / ${f2(d.b_other)} (other)${d.b_source === "pooled (sector F < 10)" ? " (sector first stage weak: pooled used)" : ""}\nFTE ${s1(d.dlog_fte)}, staff ${s1(d.dlog_staff)}`}))]
  })}<p class="cs-note">${wOK ? "" : "<b>Only the v1 headcount split with the control function has an enrollment-weighted version; showing unweighted.</b> "}Enrollment part = (β<sub>pop</sub> − 1) × population-driven change + (β<sub>other</sub> − 1) × all other enrollment change; staff growth beyond enrollment is the remainder (hover for the elasticities). The headline uses the pooled control-function elasticities for each measure (faculty FTE 0.65 / 0.60, non-faculty FTE 0.65 / 0.47): faculty FTE 11.0 = 7.1 + 3.9, non-faculty FTE 17.3 = 9.6 + 7.8. With the FE or 2SLS elasticities, non-faculty growth beyond enrollment runs from 7.8 to 11.1. Pooled rows apply one elasticity to each sector's own enrollment changes, so read sector splits as approximate; the sector-specific rows use each sector's own elasticity (pooled where the sector's first stage is weak). At public research universities enrollment grew, so the enrollment part is slightly negative and growth beyond enrollment slightly exceeds the rise (there faculty grew more than non-faculty). At community colleges faculty FTE tracked enrollment (little beyond it) while non-faculty FTE grew well beyond it.</p>`;
}
```

::: {.cs-box}
#### A hypothesis that didn't hold: national online providers
```{ojs}
{
  const g = (sg, t, spec = "main") => OP.find(d => d.sg === sg && d.term === t && d.spec === spec);
  const cc = g("cc", "X");
  return md`If large national online universities (Western Governors, Southern New Hampshire, Arizona State's online campus and 48 others) were pulling students from nearby campuses, colleges in states where those providers grew fastest should have lost more, especially colleges serving older, part-time and commuting students. They didn't. Non-traditional and local colleges did not lose more where exposure was higher, and placebo pre-trends are flat. Community colleges in high-exposure states lost ${f2(cc.coef)} (SE ${f2(cc.se)}) log points per percentage point of exposure, about −7 log points in all, but the more local colleges lost less, not more. **The hypothesis is not supported.**`;
}
```
:::

::: {.cs-note}
**Data.** IPEDS fall enrollment and Human Resources (FY2024 NCES provisional); SEER county population by single year of age; BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics; IPEDS distance-education counts. Gravity population instrument with county base years 1987 and 2002; standard errors clustered by state. Sector groups pool public master's and bachelor's colleges (regional publics) and private master's and bachelor's colleges.
:::
